detail.longDescription: I am working on a Python Selenium application that monitors an exam registration website. I am getting a 403 Forbidden response when the site is opened through Selenium, while the exact same URL opens normally in regular Chrome on my PC. Environment: - Python 3.12 - Selenium - Google Chrome - ChromeDriver / Selenium Manager - Application is deployed on Railway - Railway has a static outbound IPv4 address - Chrome version on Railway: 153.0.8010.36 The problem is: 1. Normal Chrome on my PC: The website opens normally. 2. Selenium with headed Chrome: The page returns: "Forbidden Your request was forbidden by the server." 3. Selenium with headless Chrome: Same 403 Forbidden response. 4. Selenium with a clean/new Chrome profile: Same 403 response. 5. I also tested through proxies, but Chrome then sometimes reports: ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES 6. I also verified that Chrome itself is installed correctly on Railway and Selenium can start the browser. 7. Chrome/driver versions appear compatible. The Selenium page diagnostic shows: URL: https://www.goethe.de/ins/pk/en/spr/prf/gzsd1.cfm TITLE: Forbidden BODY: Forbidden Your request was forbidden by the server. The Selenium application uses normal delays between actions and waits for page elements rather than sending requests continuously. I have already tested: - headed vs headless - clean Chrome profile - direct connection - proxy connection - Railway static outbound IP - Chrome/driver compatibility What I would like to understand is: Why would a website return 403 to Selenium while the same URL works in normal Chrome? What legitimate diagnostics can I use to determine whether the 403 is caused by: - the server/network, - Railway's outbound connection, - HTTP/TLS differences, - Selenium/WebDriver configuration, - Chrome configuration, - proxy configuration, - or something else? I am looking for troubleshooting/diagnostic advice rather than CAPTCHA or security-bypass techniques. Any suggestions for determining the exact source of the 403 would be appreciated.
